diagnostics.history_context:
Student: My semester GPA is 3.10 and my cumulative GPA is 1.99.Have I met the semester-GPA condition for merit-scholarship continuation?
Assistant (context only): you have met the semester-GPA condition for merit-scholarship continuation because your semester GPA of 3.10 is 3.0 or higher . However, the rules also specify that internal sponsorships are suspended if the student's cumulative GPA (CGPA) falls below the minimum specified to avoid warning (which is a CGPA of 2.00) and shall be restored upon getting out of warning by improvement in CGPA  .

Student: Does that mean my financial support must continue?
Assistant (context only): your financial support does not automatically continue under those conditions . While maintaining a semester GPA of 3.0 or higher satisfies the continuation requirement for merit scholarships , internal sponsorships are also subject to the rule that they are suspended if a student's cumulative GPA (CGPA) falls below the minimum specified to avoid warning (which is a CGPA of 2.00), and they shall be restored only upon getting out of warning by improving the CGPA  . Because your CGPA is 1.99, it is below the 2.00 threshold required to avoid academic warning  , meaning internal sponsorships are suspended .

**Related conditions and exceptions from the retrieved sources:**

> This scholarship is for four years of un -interrupted studies with standard courses (core and elective), labs and final year projects of the degree offered by the department in a semester to a batch with a specified number of total credit hours and is equal to the full tuition fee. 

> A student registering for less or more credit hours than the total specified number of credit hours shall not be eligible for Merit Scholarship. 

> Student must not have failed, repeated or withdrawn from a course in that semester 

Student: Now change only my cumulative GPA to exactly 2.00.
Assistant (context only): With a semester GPA of 3.10 and a cumulative GPA (CGPA) of 2.00, you have met the semester-GPA continuation requirement for merit scholarships, and your financial support is not suspended because your CGPA is no longer below the 2.00 threshold required to avoid academic warning    . 

Specifically:
* **Merit-Scholarship Continuation:** Continuation of a merit scholarship is subject to maintaining a semester GPA of 3.0 or higher  . Since your semester GPA is 3.10, you satisfy this threshold  .
* **Financial Support / Internal Sponsorships & Study Loans:** Internal sponsorships and financial assistance loans are suspended if a student's CGPA falls below the minimum specified to avoid warning (which is a CGPA of 2.00)   . Because your CGPA is now exactly 2.00, it is not below the warning threshold, meaning your financial support is not subject to suspension under this rule    .

Student: I receive financial assistance. Can I withdraw from a course?
Assistant (context only): Students receiving any form of financial support are not allowed to withdraw from any course . 

Specifically, the course withdrawal rules and procedure include:
* **Eligibility:** Students on any form of financial support are not allowed to withdraw from any course . Furthermore, first-semester students are not allowed to withdraw from any course unless necessitated by unavoidable circumstances .
* **Approval & Countersignature:** Applications for withdrawal from a course must be countersigned by the student's parent or guardian and approved by the Head of Department (HoD) . For first-semester unavoidable circumstances, the request must be approved by the Director of the campus .
* **Deadline:** The deadline to withdraw from a course is the last day of the makeup week of every semester .
* **Fee & Grade Implications:** Fees are not refunded for a withdrawn course . A grade of "W" will be awarded and will appear on the transcript, but it will not affect the CGPA .

Student: Different topic: can I renew a borrowed book?
Assistant (context only): Renewal of borrowed books cannot be claimed as a right, and priority would be given to those on the waiting list, if any . Additionally, the library has the right to recall the material on a when and where required basis . Undergraduate borrowers have a maximum renewal limit of 02 times, with a loan period of 02 weeks per loan .

Student: What if someone else is waiting for that book?
Assistant (context only): Renewal of a borrowed book cannot be claimed as a right, and priority would be given to those on the waiting list if any .

Assistant (context only): Students receiving any form of financial support are not allowed to withdraw from any course .

* **Eligibility:** Students on any form of financial support are not allowed to withdraw from any course . Furthermore, first-semester students are not allowed to withdraw from any course unless necessitated by unavoidable circumstances .
* **Approval & Countersignature:** Applications for withdrawal from a course must be countersigned by the student's parent or guardian and approved by the Head of Department (HoD) . For first-semester unavoidable circumstances, the request must be approved by the Director of the campus .
* **Deadline:** The deadline to withdraw from a course is the last day of the makeup week of every semester .
* **Fee & Grade Implications:** Fees are not refunded for a withdrawn course . A grade of "W" will be awarded and will appear on the transcript, but it will not affect the CGPA .

Computing labs, engineering labs, common rooms, sports grounds, fitness center, medical

2. Grading and GPA Calculations 
Grade Point Average 
2.1  The Grade Point Average (GPA) provides a continuous scale 
for grades earned. Two types of averages are computed for 
the grades obtained by a student, the Semester Grade Point 
Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative G rade Point Average 
(CGPA). The SGPA indicates the GPA of courses completed in 
a semester, whereas the CGPA provides the cumulative GPA 
of all courses completed so far by a student. 
Interpretation of Letter Grades 
2.2  Interpretation of Letter Grades is as follows: 
Grade Interpretation 
A+ Outstanding 
A, A- Excellent 
B+, B, B- Good 
C+, C Adequate 
C-, D+, D Pass, the student may repeat the course 
F Fail 
FA Fail due to shortage of attendance 
I Incomplete 
W Withdrawn 
S Satisfactory 
U Unsatisfactory

Grade Points 
2.3  The points for each letter grade are given as follows: 
Grade Points Grade Points 
A+ 4.00 C+ 2.33 
A 4.00 C 2.00 
A- 3.67 C- 1.67 
B+ 3.33 D+ 1.33 
B 3.00 D 1.00 
B- 2.67 F 0.00 
GPA Calculation 
2.4  SGPA is calculated as follows: 
SGPA = (P1*C1 + P2*C2 + P3*C3 + P4*C4)/C 
2.5  Where P1, P2, P3 and P4 are the grade points earned in 
courses, while C1, C2, C3, C4 are the credit hours of respective 
course studied in the s emester and C is the number  of total 
credits attempted in the semester, that is, C= C1+C2+C3+C4. 
2.6  CGPA is calculated as the weighted average for all semesters 
cumulatively using grade points of a ll the courses taken by a 
student.

turns.question: My friend says all students can get a single hostel room.
turns.answer: Not all students can get single-occupancy hostel rooms [S1]. As per policy, single- and double-occupancy rooms are reserved exclusively for graduating batches with top CGPAs or for students with valid medical reasons endorsed by the Medical Officer, the Hall Management Committee, and approved by the competent authority, while new batches are accommodated in shared rooms [S1].

FAQs ABOUT HOSTELS
Are Single- And Double-Occupancy Rooms Available For All Students?
As per policy, single- and double-occupancy rooms are reserved exclusively for graduating
batches with top CGPAs or for students with valid medical reasons. This medical reason shall
be valid after the endorsement of the Medical Officer, the Hall Management Committee, & approval
from the competent authority. The new batch will be accommodated in shared rooms.
How Can I Join The Gym Facility At Hostels?
Students may avail the hostel gym facility by paying a maintenance fee of Rs. 5,000 per
semester or Rs. 2,000 per month, along with a one-time registration fee of Rs. 1,000.

segregation and security standards.

residential needs of students. Each room is equipped with essential furniture such as

FAQs
Is There Any Information For The Parent Of A Student?
CFD campus welcomes parents at the campus on any day for student's academic information
or record discussion. It is suggested that parents must visit the student's profile on LMS.
Do Employers Recruit Students On Campus?
The career services Office regularly shares available employment opportunities offered by
leading organizations. It actively arranges recruitment drives and professional development
seminars. Campus annually organizes the Job Fair to facilitate the recruitment process
of our graduating batch.
How Do I Contact CFD Campus Alumni?
You can communicate with the OSAF (Old Student Association of FAST NUCES).
What Sort Of Clubs And Societies Can I Join?
several societies, covering a wide variety of interests, are available for students to join or
attend. Social, sports, and literature based clubs also exist. The campus also provides you
clubs like ACM and IEEE that bridge between academic and industry.
Who Should I Contact In Case Of Any Complaint/ Harassment Or Ragging?
The issue can be taken up with hostel warden or batch advisors. In case of serious issues you
can email to HoD/Director Campus.
What Is The Social Life At Campus?
Campus organizes multiple events annually such as orientation ceremony, welcome parties
for newcomers, recreational tours, technical competitions, sports events, annual leagues,
farewells and much more. The region's biggest Olympiad DAIRA is organized every year.
What Are Allied Facilities At Campus?
Computing labs, engineering labs, common rooms, sports grounds, fitness center, medical
center, mosque, library, discussion rooms, transportation, hostel, and research labs.
